_comment: Measured locally with `bazel --nohome_rc test --config=doltserver-proxied
//cmd/bd:bd_proxied_test` -- the exact config bazel.yml's proxied-server tier
uses, including `-test.parallel=4` (local sandboxed execution only; no remote
executor or cache flags were configured for this measurement run; Bazel's own
--remote_download_regex etc. in that config do not enable remote execution
without --config=remote-exec, which was not passed).
This replaces an earlier capture that used `-test.parallel=1` (serial). That
methodology avoided double-counting a parallel subtest group's own duration on
top of its children's, which was a genuine bug in an even earlier pass -- but
serial timings do not model this lane, which always runs at parallel=4, and an
independent re-review measured near-zero correlation (r=0.08) between the
serial-derived predicted shard load and actual parallel=4 wall time. These
values are each a clean, single-job (no other concurrent heavy bazel/dolt job
intentionally started on the box; see below), parallel=4 top-level test's own
<testsuite time=...> attribute from a single fresh, manifest-aligned 30-shard
sweep where every shard ran its exact assigned test set once (no duplicates,
no gaps -- see scripts/ci/gen_proxied_shard_manifest.py's exact-once coverage
check). A top-level Go test's <testsuite time> already reflects, not adds to,
its own parallel children's wall-clock time, so no leaf-summation step was
needed this time: every one of the 176 discovered tests completed inside a
single shard run with errors="0" (none needed Bazel's per-target default
timeout worked around via a separate `bazel run`, unlike the prior capture).
`seconds_per_init_fallback` is the weighted average seconds-per-init over
every measured test in this file (sum of all durations / sum of all inits),
used only for a brand-new test with no entry yet (see
scripts/ci/gen_proxied_shard_manifest.py's discover_inits_cost()). It dropped
from the serial capture's 39.7275 to this capture's lower value because
parallel=4 genuinely shortens most tests' wall time relative to inits count;
this is expected, not a data error.
This file still does not claim shard totals land within a few seconds of each
other -- see .github/workflows/bazel.yml for the current, honest expected
spread for the 30-shard proxied lane, now also derived from this same sweep.
The box this was measured on also runs other engineers'/agents' unrelated
Bazel jobs; this capture was not run with exclusive use of the machine, only
with no other *intentional, task-related* heavy bazel/dolt job started
concurrently by this task. Absolute seconds may be inflated by ambient
contention; relative ordering between tests, which is what LPT packing
actually depends on, should still be far more representative than the
discarded serial data (confirmed: 30/30 shards passed, 0 failures, 0 races,
with the two blocker fixes -- shortSocketPath and cmd.Cancel -- applied).
Regenerate with a local `bazel --nohome_rc test --config=doltserver-proxied
//cmd/bd:bd_proxied_test --build_event_json_file=<path>` sweep, then pull
each shard's bazel-testlogs test.xml <testsuite time> per top-level test --
not from downloaded CI artifacts -- so the parallel=4, CI-representative
methodology above is applied consistently.
Added after that sweep: TestProxiedServerOutageReconnectAcceptanceMatrix (80.0,
renamed into the discovery pattern once its outage bound was fixed). Not a
single sweep's value: local --config=doltserver-proxied runs measured it at
55-79 s alone, 60-70 s inside its shard, and a reviewer's 68-109 s under load;
80 s is a rounded middle of that spread. seconds_per_init_fallback was
recomputed to include it.
